D019-D020_h001.question:
I’ve been having a hard time since… well, it’s been a few weeks now, maybe less than a month? It’s hard to keep track. Working in hospice, I’ve seen a lot, but one of the patients’ passing hit differently this time. I can’t shake it. Some nights I sleep for eight hours, but I wake up feeling like I haven’t slept at all—drained, heavy, like my body didn’t rest.  

And then, out of nowhere, I’ll be at work changing linens or giving meds, and suddenly I’m back there—seeing her face, hearing the monitor flatline, feeling that same knot in my chest. It’s not like a memory; it’s like it’s happening again. I freeze for a second, and then I’m back. It’s brief, but terrifying.  

I don’t know how long this has been going on. A couple of weeks? Maybe three weeks exactly—it blurs. I don’t want to talk about it much. I just keep hoping it’ll pass. I still go to work. I still do the job. But something feels… off. Like I’m not all here. I used to be able to compartmentalize, but now I just feel stranded between the living and the dying—and I don’t know where I belong.
D019-D020_h001.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h001.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h002.question:
I’ve been having a really hard time sleeping lately—just can’t stay asleep. I’ll wake up every couple of hours, and then my mind starts racing. It’s like my brain won’t shut off. And when I do sleep, I keep having these dreams... they’re always about the lab. Specifically, that case from a few weeks ago—the burned body we recovered from the apartment fire. I wasn’t the first responder, but I processed the evidence, and there was this one personal item… a child’s shoe, partially melted. I can’t get it out of my head.

The dreams aren’t exact replays, but the feeling is there—the heat, the smoke smell, my hands shaking while I bagged the piece. I’ll jolt awake, heart pounding, and just lie there until morning light. I’ve started avoiding the storage room at work. It’s not that I can’t do my job, but sometimes I feel… detached, like I’m watching myself from outside. I know it hasn’t been *that* long since it happened—maybe a little over two weeks?—but I don’t know if this is just me needing time, or if something’s really off. I don’t want to overreact, but I can’t shake the sense that I’m not quite back to myself.
D019-D020_h002.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h002.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h003.question:
I’ve been having a hard time since that call a few weeks back—the one where the little girl was trapped in the car after the crash. I kept my voice calm on the line, but… I can’t shake it. I wake up two or three times every night, and even when I sleep seven or eight hours, I feel completely drained by the morning. It’s like my body never resets.  

Certain sounds set me off now—like when the scanner crackles or someone mentions car accidents in conversation. Last week, a coworker played a voicemail prank, and the sudden tone made me jump so hard I nearly dropped my coffee. My heart was racing for ten minutes. I’ve started dreading shift changes, especially when we get calls near that intersection.  

I don’t know if it’s normal to still feel this way. I haven’t missed work, and I’m getting through the shifts, but it’s like everything’s a little sharper, louder. I keep replaying the girl’s voice. I thought I’d bounce back by now. But instead, it feels like the job—something I’ve always handled—is starting to wear me down in a new way. I just don’t feel like myself.
D019-D020_h003.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h003.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h004.question:
I’ve been having a hard time sleeping lately—like, not just tossing and turning, but my mind just won’t shut off. I lie there for hours, heart racing, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen. It’s been like this most nights, but it’s worse if I even hear a truck backfire or see a yellow safety vest hanging up. Last week, I was on the job and a crane swung a beam close by—normal worksite stuff, really—and I froze. My chest tightened, I couldn’t breathe right, and all I could see was that day last month when the scaffold gave way. No one died, and I walked away, but… it changed something. 

I keep replaying it—not the fall itself, but the sound right before. Now, even when someone drops a tool or shouts "brace!", my body tenses like I’m back there. I tell myself, *It’s fine, it’s over*, but my body doesn’t listen. 

I don’t know how long it’s been—maybe a couple of weeks? Less than a month, definitely. I haven’t missed work, not yet, but I’m not sleeping, and I feel jumpy all the time. I just want to feel normal on the rig again.
D019-D020_h004.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h004.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h005.question:
I’ve been waking up around 4 every morning, same time I start prep at the restaurant, and I just… can’t fall back asleep. My mind’s already racing—thoughts about the incident, then about work, then back again. Even when I’m exhausted, my body won’t let me rest. It’s been like this for… I don’t know, a few weeks? Maybe less. Hard to track.

There was this one night—there was an accident in the kitchen. A fire, really bad. Someone got hurt. I wasn’t burned, but… I see it when I close my eyes. Smell the smoke even now, sometimes, when someone char-grills. Last week, a smoke alarm went off in the pantry—just a battery test—and I couldn’t breathe. Had to step outside. Felt like I was back there.

I keep replaying it. Not every second, but when it hits, it’s like I’m frozen. My hands shake. My wife says I’ve been distant, that I flinch when she touches my shoulder from behind. I hate that I’m like this. It’s affecting dinner service, and my sous chef’s noticing. I just want to get back to normal, but I don’t know what normal is right now.
D019-D020_h005.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h005.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h006.question:
I’ve been waking up around 4 every morning—sometimes earlier—and once I’m up, my mind just races. I lie there going over everything, and sleep won’t come back. It’s been like this for... I don’t know, a few weeks? Hard to say exactly. I work long hours as a robotics engineer, and lately I’ve been avoiding team meetings. I used to enjoy solving complex problems, but now nothing really feels satisfying, not even finishing a tough project or when my daughter draws me a picture. I just can’t access that feeling of joy anymore.

There was this incident—something at work a while back, a safety scare involving one of the prototype systems. I remember the alarms going off, the shouting, but some parts are just... blank. I can’t recall how I got out of the bay, or what someone said right after. It’s strange—I remember the smell of burning plastic, but not the minutes just after. 

My wife notices I’m distant. I don’t snap, I just... shut down. I don’t know if this started right after the event or if it crept in. It’s not like I’m haunted every hour, but something’s off. I can’t get back to how I was.
D019-D020_h006.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h006.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h007.question:
I’ve been having these awful dreams—reliving the same thing over and over, waking up drenched in sweat, heart racing. It started not too long ago, but I can’t even say exactly when. The weird part is, I can’t really remember much about what happened. There are big chunks missing—like my mind just… blanked it out. I know *something* happened, something bad, but the details slip away every time I try to grab them.

During the day, I feel numb, like I’m moving through thick air. I used to take pride in balancing my drawer perfectly at work—my manager even mentioned it last week—but I didn’t feel anything. No satisfaction, no sense of accomplishment, nothing. My husband tries to talk to me, but I just shut down or walk away.

I haven’t been sleeping well, obviously, and I’m on edge all the time. But some days feel almost normal, and then others just crash down. I don’t know if this is supposed to take longer to figure out, or if maybe I’m just supposed to get over it. It hasn’t even been a full month, I think? Maybe it’s too soon to say what’s really going on.
D019-D020_h007.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h007.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h008.question:
I’ve been having these horrible dreams—reliving pieces of it, over and over. I wake up drenched, heart racing, like I’m right back in the car, but then… some of it just isn’t there. I remember the rain, the headlights coming fast, the sound of crumpling metal—but what happened right after the impact? Nothing. It’s like a wall. My husband says I’ve been distant, like I’m present but not really *here*. I’ll laugh at something my coworker says, then two minutes later feel completely hollow, like joy just… short-circuited.  

Work’s been harder. I’m supposed to be in front of doctors, confident, sharp—but I keep spacing out during presentations, like my mind’s somewhere else. I don’t know how long this’s been going on—weeks, maybe? Less than a month? I didn’t think it was this bad until my sister asked if something happened. I told her about the accident, but even saying it out loud feels… disconnected. Like it happened to someone else.  

I keep wondering—am I just not coping, or is this normal? Everyone says give it time, but I don’t feel like I’m moving forward. Just… stuck in pieces of it.
D019-D020_h008.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h008.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h009.question:
I’ve been having trouble since… well, it happened a few weeks ago. I don’t really know exactly when. Working nights, you lose track. After the incident on the platform—when that man fell in front of the train—I keep sleeping, but not like I used to. I’ll get home at 7 a.m. and crash for ten, twelve hours straight, sometimes even nap in the afternoon if I can’t get out of bed. But it’s not restful. I wake up tired, like my body’s heavy.

Parts of it come back in pieces. I remember his shoes—blue sneakers, one untied—but I can’t recall if he was wearing a coat. The sound, though… that’s clear. I don’t know why some things stick and others don’t.

I finished cleaning the last car that night—supervisor said I did good under pressure. But it didn’t feel like anything. I’ve always taken pride in my work. Not anymore. It’s like there’s a gap where that feeling used to be. I show up, I do the job, but nothing matters.

I just can’t seem to settle. Not panicked, not sad—just… empty. Like I’m watching myself from far away. I thought I’d feel better by now, but time doesn’t feel like it’s helping.
D019-D020_h009.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h009.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h010.question:
I’ve been waking up every morning around 3 or 4 a.m., wide awake, heart racing, like my body’s ready even when my mind isn’t. It’s been happening off and on for… I don’t know, a few weeks maybe? It’s hard to track. I run a caseload of trauma survivors, so my days start heavy and end heavier. 

There’s this… blankness now, though. Like something shifted inside me. I hugged my sister last weekend—she was crying, thanking me for being there—and I just stood there. No warmth, no pull. I love her, I *know* I do, but I couldn’t feel it. It scared me. 

And parts of that night… I can’t reach them. I remember the headlights, the sound, getting out of the car, but then—nothing. A gap. I’ve tried to piece it together, but it’s like my mind refuses. The thing is, I’m not even sure when it happened exactly. A while back? Recently? I’ve been so scattered. I keep thinking, *Was it bad enough? Am I just falling apart from work?* Because I’m not sure if this is grief, guilt… or something else I can’t name.
D019-D020_h010.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h010.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h011.question:
I’ve just been feeling so off lately—more than I can explain. Little things like what to wear or what to make for dinner have become overwhelming. I’ll stand in front of my closet for ages, second-guessing myself, and my husband has noticed I keep asking him to decide things for me. At work, I find myself staring at a spreadsheet, knowing I need to finish it, but I can’t bring myself to pick which number to adjust first.

I also can’t seem to relax in public. In the grocery store or at a restaurant, I’m always aware of where the doors are, who’s around me. I check over my shoulder more than I used to. And if someone touches my arm unexpectedly—like a coworker trying to get my attention—I jump. It’s embarrassing, really. My heart races, and I feel like I can’t catch my breath.

This started… well, I’m not sure exactly when. Not long ago, but it doesn’t feel brand new either. I haven’t been sleeping well. Nothing terrible happened—nothing I can pinpoint, at least—just this lingering sense that something’s wrong, even though everything should be fine.
D019-D020_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h011.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h012.question:
I’ve been feeling completely on edge for a while now—can’t really put a date on it, but it’s been weeks, maybe? It’s like my brain won’t shut off. Even at home, just sitting on the couch, I can’t relax. My shoulders are always tight, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen.  

Little things throw me—my phone buzzing, a car horn outside—sometimes I flinch so hard I drop what I’m holding. It’s embarrassing. At work, I design engine systems, and I used to make decisions fast, but now I’ll stare at two coffee options for ten minutes, second-guessing myself. What if I pick wrong? What if it messes up my day?  

I don’t know what set this off, honestly. Nothing major happened—no accident, no loss—just sort of… crept in. I used to like going out, but now I avoid crowded places. Too loud. Too much. My focus at work is slipping, and I’m missing deadlines. My manager asked if I’m okay. I don’t know how to answer.  

I haven’t been sleeping well, either—light, restless, like I’m listening for something. But no memory of a trauma or anything. Just this constant hum of tension, like my body forgot how to stand down.
D019-D020_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h012.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h013.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a while now—just can’t seem to think straight. My thoughts feel foggy, like I’m walking through a haze even when I’m wide awake. At work, I’ll be reviewing site plans and suddenly realize I’ve read the same sentence three times and still don’t know what it says. It’s frustrating because precision matters in landscape architecture, and I’ve always prided myself on attention to detail.

I also catch myself constantly watching my surroundings—especially when I’m out, like at a client site or even just walking through a parking lot. My eyes dart to sudden movements, shadows, people coming around corners. If someone walks up behind me too quickly, I nearly jump out of my skin. My husband noticed—I used to be easygoing, but now he’ll say, “You’re looking over your shoulder again.”

I don’t know what set it off exactly. Nothing dramatic comes to mind, no single event. Just this creeping sense that something isn’t safe, even though logically, I know I’m okay. It’s been weeks—maybe a little less—hard to say. But it’s not like I’ve been through anything extreme. At least, I don’t think so.
D019-D020_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h013.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h014.question:
I’ve been struggling to think clearly lately—everything feels foggy, like I’m moving through water. At work, I’ll read the same email three times and still not absorb it, which is scary because I’m managing shipments across four regions, and one mistake can ripple out fast. I can’t focus like I used to. My wife’s noticed too—she says I’m distant, like I’m somewhere else.  

I’ve started scanning rooms the second I walk in—where are the exits, who’s near me, could I get out fast if something happened? It’s automatic, but exhausting. I can’t turn it off, even at home. The worst part is if someone touches me unexpectedly—my coworker patted my shoulder the other day and I nearly jumped out of my skin. I could see he was startled by my reaction.  

I don’t know when this started exactly. A few weeks? Maybe less. There was something—a situation—but it wasn’t like, *war* or anything extreme. Still, it’s changed how I move through the world. I just keep thinking: *What if it happens again?* But I can’t even say for sure that what I’m feeling is “about” that thing. Maybe it’s just stress. Or maybe I’m falling apart for no reason.
D019-D020_h014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h014.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h015.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a little while now—hard to say exactly how long. It’s like my head’s in a fog, you know? I’ll be rehearsing, and suddenly I can’t remember the measure I just played. My thoughts feel… thick, like I’m trying to swim through syrup. It’s scary, honestly, because my violin used to be second nature.

Lately, I notice myself scanning the room a lot—during concerts, backstage, even at coffee shops. I keep checking where the exits are, watching people’s hands, flinching if someone slams a door or if a cymbal crashes unexpectedly. Last week, a colleague dropped a music stand and I swear I jumped out of my skin—felt my whole body jerk. It’s embarrassing, especially in front of the others.

I don’t know what set this off. Nothing major happened, not like… not like something that would explain all this. Some days I feel almost normal, but then a sound—a siren, a loud laugh—and I’m right back there, tense, on edge. I haven’t missed work, but I’m just… not myself.
D019-D020_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h015.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h016.question:
I’ve been having a tough time lately—can’t get this thing out of my head. It happened… I don’t know, a few weeks ago, maybe a little longer. There was an accident at a job site—not me, thank God, but it was bad. I keep seeing flashes of it when I’m just sitting there, trying to relax. Outta nowhere. Same image, like a loop. It knocks the wind out of me every time.

I’ve been steering clear of that part of town now. Even turned down a call near that intersection. If someone mentions it, or if I see an ambulance go by, I feel my chest tighten. I’ve stopped going near the warehouse district altogether. Doesn’t matter if it’s a pain to explain to the boss.

The weirdest part? I can’t remember much about that day—not all of it. It’s like parts just… aren’t there. I know I was there, I know what I saw at first, but after that? Nothing solid. It’s frustrating. My wife says I’ve been off—short-tempered, quiet—or just zoning out during dinner. I just don’t know how to make it stop.
D019-D020_h016.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h016.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h017.question:
I’ve been off ever since it happened. I can’t even tell you exactly when—days blur together now. I work as an accountant, so numbers used to be my safe place, but lately I can’t focus. If someone mentions the accident or I see something on the news—just a glimpse of brake lights or a siren—my chest tightens and I start shaking, like my body remembers before my mind does. I don’t want to talk about it. I avoid calling my husband, even though we live in the same house. It’s not that I don’t love him; I just can’t stand the look in his eyes when he asks, “Are you okay?”  

There are gaps, too—whole pieces of that day I can’t reach. I know I was in the car, and then I wasn’t. After that? Fog. Sometimes I think I’m remembering, but it slips away. I don’t cry. I don’t scream. I just… disengage. I keep waiting to feel like myself again, but I don’t know when that was anymore. I can still go to work, file the reports, send the emails—but it feels like I’m watching someone else do it.
D019-D020_h017.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h017.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h018.question:
I’ve been having these dreams lately—same one over and over. I’m back in the server room, but it’s all wrong: flickering lights, alarms blaring, and someone’s shouting, though I can’t remember who. I wake up sweating and can’t go back to sleep. Honestly, I try not to think about that night at all. If something triggers it—a sound, the smell of burnt plastic—I shut down, change the subject, walk away. It’s like my brain just… refuses to go there.

The worst part is, I can’t even remember what happened. I know there was an incident during the fire suppression test, that the system discharged accidentally, and something went wrong with the oxygen levels. But after that—it’s like a gap. Big chunks are just gone. I’ve been told bits, but it doesn’t feel real.  

Lately, I’m short-tempered at work, tired all the time. I used to handle the night shift fine, but now I’m on edge, second-guessing every alert. I haven’t told my supervisor. I just want to get through the cycle and go home.  

I don’t know when it started, exactly. Could’ve been a few weeks. Might’ve been less. I stopped tracking after a while.
D019-D020_h018.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h018.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h019.question:
I’ve been having a hard time since that incident on the job site a while back—can’t even say exactly when it happened, honestly. My memory’s all spotty, like whole chunks are just gone. I remember the sirens, the yelling, and someone getting loaded into the ambulance, but the details around it? Nothing. I try not to go there in my head. When I do, my chest gets tight, my hands shake, and sometimes I break into a sweat for no reason. Even seeing a yellow hard hat like the one he wore—that’s enough to make me feel like I can’t breathe.  

I’ve been staying away from thoughts about it, you know? Like, I’ll switch the channel if something comes up on TV, or change the subject real quick if the guys talk about it on site. I just don’t want to feel that again. I haven’t told anyone what I saw, not really. Feels safer not to.  

It’s been messing with my focus, my sleep. I don’t know if it’s been weeks or just days. Time’s been weird. I’m still showing up to work—gotta pay the bills—but it’s getting heavier. I can’t say if it’s supposed to feel like this or if it’ll pass. Honestly, I didn’t think I needed to talk about it until now.
D019-D020_h019.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h019.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h020.question:
I’ve been having a real hard time since the accident on the job site—guy fell from a scaffold right near me. I wasn’t hit, but I saw it all. For weeks now, I keep reliving that moment—outta nowhere, like a flash, I’m right back there hearing the noise, seeing his body. It knocks the wind outta me every time. I try not to think about it, but the harder I push it away, the more it sneaks up. Honestly, I can’t remember exactly how he fell. One second he was up there, next—boom—he’s on the ground. The middle part? Blank.  

I’ve been avoiding the guys from work, even skipped a few shifts. Don’t wanna talk about it, don’t wanna hear it. Feels like if I start, I won’t stop. My chest gets tight, my hands sweat—like I’m losing it. I thought I’d shake it off by now, but it’s hanging on. I don’t know if it’s been days or weeks. I just know I’m not sleeping, not really living. I can’t tell if I’m just messed up from the shock or if I’m falling apart from stress. Feels like both… and neither.
D019-D020_h020.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h020.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h021.question: I’ve been having these flashes—like little movies I can’t turn off. A patient coding last week, the way his hand dropped when we stopped compressions, the family screaming in the hallway. I keep seeing it, even when I’m at home. It’s not like I’m reliving it, exactly, but it just pops in, and my chest gets tight. I yelled at a coworker the other day over a missing IV kit—called her irresponsible, raised my voice so much people looked. I don’t even recognize myself. I’ve always handled stress; we see tough things all the time in the ER. But this feels different. It’s only been a few days, maybe a week? Time’s been blurry. I snapped at my sister, too, over nothing. Felt bad right after, but I couldn’t seem to stop myself. I’m not sleeping well. Not because I’m scared or anything, just… restless. I keep thinking I should be able to manage this. I’m supposed to be the one helping people stay calm, not falling apart. But something feels off—like my nerves are raw. I don’t know if it’s from this one event or everything piling up. I just want it to quiet down.
D019-D020_h021.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h021.answer: C & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h022.question: I’ve always been in tune with my emotions—part of the job, really. But lately, things have been… off. Something happened a little while ago—something intense, something I can’t just shake like a bad audition. I don’t want to go into detail, but certain sounds, even a tone of voice, can knock me sideways. Once, during rehearsal, a stagehand slammed a prop door the same way, and I just froze. My chest tightened, and I had to leave the stage. I didn’t yell then, but I’ve snapped at people—my husband, my stage manager—crying, screaming, blaming them for things that aren’t their fault. It’s not like me. I’m supposed to be strong, present, *together*. But now I feel like I’m unraveling when the lights come up. I don’t know if it’s been weeks or just days—time’s been blurry. I keep thinking I should be over it by now, but I’m not. And I’m scared that if I’m not careful, I’ll lose the thing that defines me—my voice, my craft, my control.
